commenti.body:
I hope there isn't given the deaths you mention. Mi hael apted built up an amazing rapport with the interviewees respecting their wishes not to be filmed when they chose to do so. I don't think seven up would work today, too many media savvy kids would probably play it to their advantage.

I think the genuine delight of seven up was the fact that the interviewees weren't media attention grabbers, they were real people with real problems from a huge cross section of British society. Apted caught them just as British society and it's class system was changing.

I think there was a kind of new version of 7 up on channel 4 or 5, in the UK, but it lacked the sociological drive of apteds groundbreaking work. Also I think at 70 it's probably time to give the interviewees some peace.

I never knew about Nick Hitchon passing until you mentioned it. He was always very affable and open. My personal fave was the young man from Liverpool who went to Scotland lived rough for a while.

No word, but when Apted passed in 2021, [there was an article](https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/14/movies/michael-apted-up-series-future.html?smid=nytcore-android-share) at which several people mentioned his producer Claire Lewis as the obvious successor to take it over. Sounded like a resounding "maybe."

>“I could carry it on,” Lewis said, adding that it would come down to the subjects’ assent and the health of the crew. The cameraman, George Jesse Turner, and sound engineer, Nick Steer, have been with the program since “21 Up,” from 1977; the editor, Kim Horton, joined for “28 Up.”

>“None of us are spring chickens — we’re all geriatric, honestly,” Lewis said, citing her own age as “70-ish.” “We’re going to need an ambulance, if we ever did it again, to take us all around. I think we’ll just have to say we’ll wait and see.”

>Asked if she would participate without Apted, \[Jackie\] Bassett began to cry. She agreed that Lewis, who’d long had the job of keeping in touch with the cast between shoots, was the logical successor. (Walker concurred and was more enthusiastic about continuing.)

>“70 and 7 do have a good symmetry,” Bassett said. “It would definitely have to be the last one for everybody.”

Interesting, you're right that nowadays you'd probably have a lot of them gaining a following on social media so the "reveal" element of how they're getting on 7 years later would be pretty much removed.

Oh, I hadn't heard that Nick passed. The Up series is one of my favorite documentaries ever.

I don't think there'll be a new installment even though I kind of wish there was, for the same reasons OP mentions.
